Author, per the Draft Forum's new policy: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-10629348/new-draft-forum-policies authors who have not yet posted a successful mainsite article are now required to get their basic concept(s) greenlighted by two experienced reviewers in the Ideas Critique forum and/or IRC chatrooms before asking for draft feedback.

Please first go to the Ideas forum or the chat, give a quick summary (for the Ideas forum, please follow the instructions in the required reading thread) of the concept you want to write up (don't link the draft unless someone requests it), and reviewers can help you make sure that your core idea is something that will be successful with the community audience.

During the conceptualization stage, reviewers can also help by letting you know if something similar already exists on the site, and/or telling you if there are any cliches/pitfalls/other typical downvote reasons to be careful of with your particular idea. These issues are more effectively addressed earlier on in the writing process.

If you have already received the requisite greenlights, please note from whom and where you received them. If you would like to receive draft critique without going through the greenlighting process, please use the IRC chatrooms to request reviews.

Please note that greenlights are given on concepts, NOT full drafts.

item.title: Myantharun's Mandala-Manifested Meadow of Majestic, Melancholic Madness: Re: Myantharun's Mandala-Manifested Meadow of Majestic, Melancholic Madness
item.content:encoded:
+ line by line
- line by line

Special Containment Procedures: SCP-XXXX and its related anomalies are undetectable by individuals without sufficient anti-memetics training, therefore standard visual containment is not required.

You could throw in a few more details here. Maybe psychedelics or some other drug or circumstance allows people to see it.

Description: SCP-XXXX is a red mandala that has presence on a global scale and manifests in any population center, regardless of population size.

I think this one might be phrased better as “SCP-XXXX Is an anomalous mandala that has been observed appearing in multiple population centers.” or something like that

SCP-XXXX-1 is largely comprised of a meadow with an abundance of grass and blooming flowers with warm colors. It frequently changes in topography and incorporates structures and large-scale events of mass hysteria from reality.

Are these reenactments of the events? Is this a time jumping thing?

SCP-XXXX-2 is an entity of varying form that is located in SCP-XXXX-1. MTF Omicron Rho ("The Dream Team") discovered SCP-XXXX-2 in their deployment into SCP-XXXX-1. See addenda.

An “Entity of Varying form” is a very loose description. Do they know the entity is the same entity as before because it’s sapient and speaks to them or something?

Discovery: SCP-XXXX's first documented influence was in the South Florida Baptist Church located on Belvedere Road. When the congregation underwent substantial changes in behavior while in prayer.

You might want to include a town name here. Also, perhaps “While in prayer” could be replaced with “while the parishioners were praying”

Several individuals rose from their benches and sprinted down the middle aisle, screaming in the manner of chimpanzees. Another significant portion of the congregation bit the wooden pews in an attempt to consume portion of the marble that were comprised of.

Did the foundation discover this due to installed CCTV cameras? Witness reports?

After three more similar incidents, the Foundation dispatched field agents to survey the surroundings.

Honestly I could see them doing an investigation after this happened once.

their comms devices drenched

“their comms devices were discovered drenched”

. Experimental Foundation technology was used to record low quality and incomplete video footage of the events that transpired.

This could use a rephrasing, it sounds like the foundation was trying to collect low quality and incomplete video footage the way it’s phrased now

All nun in the church: Meow!

“Nuns”

Opening is not geographically part of any rock formation

“The opening resembles no known rock formation”

“Movement appears in the distance”

“Movement is detected”

<The individuals in the Foundation fatigues have no hands or feets; their legs and arms end in [REDACTED] and they levitate and float towards Myantharun at high speeds.>

Redactions are to be used quite sparingly. Is this one absolutely necessary?

The tip of the creature reaches for a Mandala hovering above in mid-air, burrows into it and leaves.

“And vanishes” or “And disappears” might be better.

Video feed abruptly changes to a long brick road with tanks and nazis marching towards Hero on both sides.

You might consider replacing Nazis with “Nazi stormtroopers” or something more specific like that.

CONSIDERATIONS:

I’ll admit… I’m not sure what’s going on here. I understand that there’s a group a dreams associated with this snake vomiting guy that can transfer the hallucinations over to reality, but other than that I’m a bit lost as to what’s going on. A lot of the imagery in the skip is nice and surreal though and I think this could be fun if we had a bit more of an idea as to what was happening.

item.title: Dysphoric Flesh: Re: Dysphoric Flesh
item.content:encoded:
I feel like I should put something here and uh I have now nice

[+] Overall
[-] Overall

I’m…not sure about this as a whole. My central concern is that the way the notes plays out feels…predictable? The emotional beats within are like, not badly done but they are done in a way that just kinda feels very expected?

The ending stands out as odd: the survival of Leif isn’t necessarily bad but it kinda, feels unimpactful in a way I can’t quite put my finger on? I think it’s because post the notes, there’s nothing really like, establishing that they might be dead: the ‘originally assumed to be a suicide note’ implies it isn’t, which in turn implies they aren’t dead, so there’s no like, stomach drop ‘are they…are they dead’ followed by subversion when they aren’t. Technically the discovery section opens with the implication they are dead but it feels like this needs a callback to that first before it can be subverted for the emotions to hit: like, if the suicide note was found and there was mention of a funeral say, there was some…minor thing to allow the emotions to hit, and then the discovery of them being found?

Even then, the relatively pedestrian nature of the notes might be an issue; but it’s possible this is just me having read too many scps and being generally jaded as a whole rather than an actual issue: if you’re getting positive feedback on this, it’s probably fine?

[-] Overall
[+] Line By Line
[-] Line By Line

Gonna note that I can miss stuff; flag things which are right as being wrong and indeed flag things which are deliberately wrong.
I'll likely use strikethrough to indicate stuff to remove and green text to indicate stuff to add.

Subjects believed to be instances of SCP-XXXX-2 are to be re-located to Foundation emergency clinics immediately for evaluation.

Probably stylistic largely, but it feels like having ‘immediately’ right before ‘re-located’ instead would be clearer

Center subject is SCP-XXXX-2-C33, infected with an instance of SCP-XXXX. Subject furthest right is SCP-XXXX-1-C33.

This feels over long for a caption; I think the ‘infected with…SCP-XXXX’ part could be trimmed; and maybe the rest streamlined further? Though I’m not sure how easy that’d be.

Contact with SCP-XXXX-1 is to be allowed once a day for feeding purposes.

The implication to me of ‘contact’ here is ‘foundation contact’, but it seems like you mean ‘SCP-XXXX-2 contact’ and I feel like it could do with being more explicit?

If SCP-XXXX-1 cannot be used

I’m not exactly sure why but something about this doesn’t sit right with me; I’m not sure if it’s the kinda casual writing or the vagueness about why -1 couldn’t be used or what though.

SCP-XXXX eggs are summoned directly into the womb, causing the subject to become an instance of SCP-XXXX-1.

‘summoned’ feels…strangely purposeful at this point: like, summoning usually implies there’s a summoner doing it; and it feels…like an angle which never really ends up going anywhere?

It then makes its way to offspring of SCP-XXXX-1 in an approximately 200-meter radius.

I guess my question is ‘what if no-such offspring are within a 200m radius?’

SCP-XXXX will attach itself to transgender or non-binary offspring of SCP-XXXX-1, hereby referred to as SCP-XXXX-2.

I feel like this should be like…next to the previous thing about it travelling to offspring? Like, if the sentence was like “It then travels to transgender or non-binary offspring of SCP-XXXX-1 in an approximately 200m radius” say.

SCP-XXXX is considered to have entered its adult phase.
In adult SCP-XXXX instances

I’d probably be consistent as to whether this is an ‘adult phase’ or ‘adult SCP-XXXX instances’; though the repetition might feel iffy: perhaps ‘These instances…’ would be fine to start the second with?

the memetic camouflage agent changes in function. SCP-XXXX will utilize its illusory effect to conceal itself and to modify SCP-XXXX-2’s appearance.

I would probably shorten this into one sentence.

Trans-positive cultural attitudes surrounding SCP-XXXX-2 have also been liked to the incidence of SCP-XXXX death.

I…don’t dislike this as a statement or anything but it raises the question of why the Foundation aren’t like…doing more to promote trans positivity? Like it’s the kinda thing you mention offhandedly here that makes me question why there’s not a co-ordinated propaganda effort to increase trans-positivity as a containment procedure for SCP-XXXX but *shrugs*

Foundation personnel were summoned to investigate the circumstances surrounding the death of Leif Ivanovich (20) in Eugene, OR.

This feels kinda weirdly passive: who summoned the Foundation? Why did they summon the Foundation?

[-] Line By Line

item.title: The Flight of the Koalas: Re: The Flight of the Koalas
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there Veralta. Let’s take a look at your concept.

+ LBL
- LBL

Wilpena Pound

This might not be as well known a place to people outside Australia. You might want to add a clarifier after?

Sightings of "flying serpents" are to be quickly verified and acted upon.

“acted upon” is slightly vague. Do you want to give a more specific hint so we can understand the anomaly a little better?

The Foundation History Department is mandated to research texts and information

The tense here is a little inconsistent when compared to the previous sentences. I would remove “is mandated to” and simply put “will” to keep with the clinical tone.

to collect pertinent information.

Again, being specific in the conprocs goes a long way. What kind of information should the Foundation look out for? This adds to our understanding of the scp in the long run.

during 2022

Sounds a little off. You would say “during a year”, but not a specific one. Would change to “in 2022”.

two years after severe bushland fires within the region

Missing an “occurred” after “fires”.

Compiled data indicates a severe decline in population density, upwards of nearly 2,000 per week.

Nitpick, but the second part of this sentence doesn’t link to the first. “2,000” refers to the actual number, not the population density.

It is to be noted that the surviving koala population at this point numbered approximately 62,000.

The past tense of “numbered” indicates that the Foundation is writing from a place of the future? Sorry, just wanted to clarify.

Additionally, testimonies from zoos across and outside the continent indicate that their koalas have also disappeared, despite all efforts to contain or track them.

This was slightly confusing to read. Do you just mean “internationally” or “globally”?

Uluru, Wilpena Pound, Black Mountain2, Arnhem Land, and the Grampian National Park.

Again, these might be entirely foreign terms for those not familiar with Australian Geography. You might want to add qualifiers like “near Sydney” or in “New South Wales”.

Heavy rainfall would occur in tandem

Tenses need to be more consistent, I think. You’re switching between present and future perfect tense, which muddies the viewer’s sense of time.

as SCP-5870 continuously occurs.

A little awkward. You mean to say “at the rate SCP-5870 continues to occur”?

The 2020 bushfires had burned 24 percent of the eucalyptus trees, while approximately 60,000 koalas have been recorded as casualties. 84 percent of survivors have severe burns on their paws, while 31 percent had suffered from dehydration and starvation.

I’m not sure this entire section should be under the “Description” section, as it’s additional context for the anomaly, and not about the anomaly itself. You could re-classify this section as your Discovery log.

SCP-5870-1 instances, despite numerous

“being numerous”.

share striking similaries.

“similarities”. And also, similarities to what? Each other?

bullroarers

Second occurrence of a foreign term without additional context.

These were subsequently fed by the entities to arriving SCP-5870-1 instances

This is happening quite fast, making it hard to keep track of who is who. “These” meaning the nuts? “the entities” here refer to the koalas? I would break up the description and add a little more detail for pacing.

After five minutes, they flew at high speeds

Indicate direction?

which would then hold onto them

“hold” => “cling”. Might want to also specify which parts of the snakes they hold onto.

where a large levitating island, referred to as SCP-5870-2, was discovered.

Whoa, whoa. Why wasn’t this noticed before?

It is to be noted that 40 percent of the island's surface is composed of a lake.

I would remove the “It is to be noted” as this is not something particularly noteworthy.

They then reach a small lake, wherein the main dome is located at its center.

This is confusing. Is the small lake located at the center of the dome? Or is the main dome at the center?

Some of the koala groups make their way to the smaller domes, which are not located in the the lake.

I thought they were deposited at the smaller domes first? “the” is repeated.

koalas living onto them

Unclear what you mean here.

as they are spectated by other koalas.

“as” meaning “because” they are spectated? Meaning unclear.

It is notably

“notably” -> “notable”.

dyed white and yellow.

Again, why is this noteworthy?

The koalas enter the dome.

I thought we were already inside the main dome. Best to clarify earlier where the drone footage starts, and where we’re headed.

manipulated in get fleshy materials

Sorry? Is there a typo here?

After it leaves the SCP-5870-2 duplicate at Mount Warning, SCP-5870-3 has collected approximately 5,600 more koalas.

The sentence structure here is convoluted. Meaning unclear.

the Foundation has listed koalas as critically endangered

Ah? Are we in a Broken Masquerade scenario? Why is the Foundation assuring the public?

Overall, I enjoyed this exploration log, though I felt it went on a little too long and didn’t understand the significance of certain events (like the koalas and kangeroos fighting). You might also want to clarify the description to make it clear what we’re seeing, when.

mitigated these through engineering solutions.

“these” refers to? If it’s the flooding, then the tense should be changed.

10 percent of its national budget to it

“it” refers to?

approximately 115.31 million tons

tonnes of what?

35 Small Modular Reactors14.

The footnote should come after the period.

the TIMES magazine

Do you mean “Time Magazine”?

Closely cooperating with aboriginal groups such as Bundjalung, Eora, and Gamilaaray, greenery restoration programs in New South Wales and Queensland have also been successful

The subject of the sentence is not clear – who is the one “closely cooperating”?

Foundation task forces quickly mobilize. Fortunately, most Australians were celebrating the New Year inside their homes.

I don’t see the link between both sentences?

turn over a new leaf

Personally, this is a highly cliqued phrase, though I can’t say much else if it’s officially a part of lore. Consider rephrasing to simply “turn over” or “turn themselves over” to get the same effect.

+ Overall
- Overall

1. Is the pacing and narrative good enough?

Well, yeah. It was a wild ride. I’m not familiar with Aboriginal culture (like, at all), and seeing these stories come to life was eye-opening. I just hoped to understand their significance a little more. You’ve clearly done our research and included many references to the culture and origin stories. The main issue (if it really is one in the first place) is outsiders like me don’t really see the significance of the minute events / symbols / objects.

I do like the overarching narrative though of nature taking climate change into its own hands. It’s a strong and relevant message. My major concern would be the deemphasis here on the Foundation’s role in the entire article. Basically, we’re just left as bystanders throughout the entire event, right? Which is fine if that’s what you’re going for, but removes any agency and tension from the narrative.

2. Is the worldbuilding and attention to detail decent and palatable?

Yup, as mentioned above, A good amount of detail included. Just needs to be further explained and the description clarified (who, where and when we are).

3. Does it sound too preachy?

Nope. I think the lesson is clear but not overbearing.

4. If applicable, have you noticed several problems and contradictions with Dreamtime lore and aboriginal beliefs?2

Perhaps I don’t understand the lore and beliefs in the first place. You could be more explicit in this regard, for example, providing an actual story or myth at the beginning, besides just the stone carving.

I also wasn’t clear throughout how the aboriginal community fit into the scp. There’s a passing reference to them creating posters to create awareness, but where do they fit into the story? Wouldn’t it be cool if you could show them being facilitators / active defenders of the entities as the anomalies occur. But again, I don’t want to prescribe a cultural stance for them.

Overall, I’m tending towards an up-vote. The writing is mostly clear, as are the notes and themes you seek to hit.

Thanks for sharing this with us!

item.title: Air Reconditioning Unit: Re: Air Reconditioning Unit
item.content:encoded:
Hi, thank you for your critique!

+ My response.
- Close response.

I’m not sure how to answer those questions and it’s mostly because I struggle with expressing the thoughts in my head. I have the answers and they make sense to me but writing them down is hard. But I’m going to try.

The whole piece is about the realisation that there’s an SCP that’s made fixing climate change kinda moot, it’s added it’s own irreversible and irrecoverable damage to the climate and that the world is kinda fucked. That’s what I want the reader to come away with.

I don’t know how I can make a character someone can relate to in this kind of piece. I thought I had at least on some small level. This one I really don’t know how to fix.

I want this to say a lot of things, like “hi I am a new writer but I want to be a part of this amazing community” or “this is something I have put time and effort and love into.” It’s probably not the right answer to that question but it’s the answer that feels right to me. This is my first SCP, when I’m gone this will remain as my legacy. I want this to be something people can point to and say “yep, that guy did that. It’s okay I guess.” That’s what I want it to say.

But again that’s not the answer you probably want, so let me try again. I love this SCP because it has potential. I make several references to another function of the object, which is functionally identical to what is described in the article except instead of turning oxygen into helium it turns it into carbon dioxide or water vapour, with the complexity going up the higher the input number. I want it to say there’s more to this, to make people think and imagine.

I did kinda stupidly think that maybe this could’ve been something that other people could collaborate on, creating and adding things to a list of what this SCP could make. But fears of it being compared to other open collaboration SCPs killed that idea. The testing log is the remnant of that I suppose, turned into an attempt to channel a narrative that admittedly has failed. I do understand that it’s a very dry narrative, and ditching the logs has been advised before. But I honestly don’t know how else to channel and describe a narrative through this kind of fiction, I’ve never written anything like an SCP article before so it’s all foreign to me.

item.title: Star Euthanizer: Re: Star Euthanizer
item.content:encoded:
{Placeholder}

On to the critique ->
– hide block

SPaG

On 28 August 1903, Foundation personnel educated in astrology sighted SCP-XXXX through a telescope near the Orion Arm.

This suggests that the telescope was situated in the Orion's Arm spiral arm, rather than the object was located in that sector. Additionally, "astrology" is defined by Merriam-Webster as "the divination of the supposed influences of the stars and planets on human affairs and terrestrial events by their positions and aspects". I believe the word you are looking for is "astronomy".

"sighted" is also defined as "able to see : not blind." Perhaps "observed".

Consistency/Flow

All deep-space observatories are to be monitored by satellite following standard procedure.

This could be cleaned up a bit to be more specific. It is unclear which standard procedure is being followed. Furthermore, I would assume that all deep space observations would be closely monitored by the SCPF as a matter of course.

The production and trade of new telescope parts such as refractors have been limited to companies where a sufficient number of undercover Foundation personnel are present.

This is also jumbled and unclear. What is this meant to prevent?

All images of SCP-XXXX are to be intercepted by the Foundation AI "Binary star", saved in the Foundation database, and subsequently deleted from public records.

I have a personal preference for utilizing the .aic convention. In this case, your AI would become Binary_Star.aic. I think it looks cleaner than "name", in that it specifies an entity rather than a "supposed" entity. It's all in the implication.

SCP-XXXX is the first spacecraft ever observed by the Foundation.

Non-human or non-terrestrial? Or did this observation predate Sputnik and the other Earth-based spacecraft?

Closing Remarks

There are significant errors throughout this piece, what is represented here are just a few examples. The idea is a sound one and I think the additional story told throughout the listpages is interesting. However, there are a lot of sentence structure and word choice errors that make this difficult to read.

Ping me on IRC at your leisure and we can go over more of them if you'd like.
